xwhatsapp-strokecopylinkgoogleAdd Al Jazeera on GoogleinfoEmergency service vehicles outside LRT Century Park Station in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada [File: Artur Widak/NurPhoto via Getty]By Al Jazeera Staff and APPublished On 18 Oct 202618 Oct 2026|Updated: 8 minutes agoUpdated: 8 minutes agoA major fire at a military base in the province of Alberta has caused several casualties, Canada’s defence minister said.

Fire crews scrambled late into the night on Saturday as fierce winds whipped flames beyond Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright, one of the busiest military training bases, and into the surrounding rural area.

“I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base,” Minister of National Defence David McGuinty said.

“I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory,” he said, adding that the situation was “very, very active and delicate”.

The Canadian broadcaster Global News said at least seven people were killed and dozens were injured, citing unnamed military sources.

Global News reported that a gas line or a gas well was hit during a live-fire training, causing an explosion that sparked the blaze.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said a “serious incident” had caused the fire, writing on social media: “Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected.”

A doctor at a hospital in Edmonton, 180km (112 miles) northwest of the base, told Canada’s national broadcaster that the casualties were being taken to hospitals across the city as healthcare facilities around the base were “completely overwhelmed” by the number of people needing care.

“This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton,” Dr Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, told CBC News.

“It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It’s a disaster. It’s a one in every 15-to-25-year disaster.”

The Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire crossed the base’s fence and spread rapidly in high winds.

Canadian armed forces and federal, provincial and local authorities are coordinating the emergency response, McGuinty said.

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called the fire “significant and tragic” and said it was affecting many military personnel.

Opposition Conservative leader Pierre Poilievre said he spoke to Carney and McGuinty to offer support. “Pray for Wainwright, everyone,” he wrote on social media, urging people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders.

The fire comes two days before Albertans vote on whether the province, home to about five million people, should begin the legal process towards a binding referendum on seceding from Canada.

Carney used his Thanksgiving message last week to call for national unity.
